title: On a neighbourhood of the closed subset where the derived limit lives, the complex has a single cohomology sheaf of finite presentation reducing correctly along the thickenings
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter flat.tex (More on Flatness), section 'The local structure of a finite type module'
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file flat.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: In the existence situation, with K as in the computation lemma and X_0 the closed subset of points lying over the common closed subset of Spec(A), the lemma asserts the existence of an open W containing X_0 with three properties: the cohomology of K vanishes on W except in degree 0, the resulting module F = H^0(K)|_W is of finite presentation, and F_n = F tensor O_{X_n} (statement lines 8180-8194). The proof is a pointwise reduction to an inductive statement about a complex of finite free modules: for a point x of X_0 it takes an affine open U = Spec(B), chooses a surjection P -> B with P smooth over A, and uses relative pseudo-coherence to represent Ri_*K by a bounded above complex F of finite free P-modules, after which tensoring with A_n computes the cohomology of F as M_n in degree 0 (proof lines 8203-8225). If the top nonvanishing index i is at most 0 the three properties hold outright; otherwise the rank of the differential F^{i-1} -> F^i is maximal at x, hence maximal on a neighbourhood, so after a principal localisation the map is surjective and splits, which replaces F by a shorter complex and closes by induction on i (proof lines 8226-8241). The truncation-by-splitting induction on the top index is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
